narrative.summaryIntro:
The Arulmigu Subramanya Swamy Temple at Tiruchendur, Thoothukudi district, Tamil Nadu, is dedicated to Murugan and is one of the Arupadaiveedu, the six principal abodes of the deity in Tamil Nadu. It is the only one of the six built directly on the coast, standing at the eastern edge of the town on the shores of the Bay of Bengal; the inner sanctum is a granite cave-shrine that sits below sea level.

The temple is associated with the Soorasamharam legend, in which Murugan defeated the asura Surapadman; the vanquished asura's transformation into a mango tree, which Murugan split with his spear, is said to have produced his peacock mount and rooster emblem, and the temple's principal festival re-enacts this victory. The complex is entered through a nine-tier gopuram about 48 metres (157 ft) high and is referenced as a Vaippu Sthalam in the 7th-century hymns of the Nayanar saint Appar. It is administered by the Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department and received ISO certification in 2016.
narrative.documentedHistory:
The temple is referenced as a Vaippu Sthalam in the hymns of the Nayanar saint Appar, placing devotional literature about the site as early as the 7th century CE. Tiruchendur is one of the Arupadaiveedu, the six principal shrines of Murugan in Tamil Nadu, and is unique among them for its location directly on the coast rather than on a hill.

The temple's mythology centres on the Soorasamharam, Murugan's defeat of the asura Surapadman: after Surapadman transformed into a mango tree, Murugan split it with his vel (spear), and the two halves are said to have become his vahana (the peacock) and the emblem on his flag (the rooster). This episode is enacted annually at the temple's principal festival.

The complex measures roughly 91 metres north–south by 65 metres east–west, with a nine-tier gopuram about 48 metres (157 ft) high; the sanctum itself is a granite rock-cut shrine that lies below sea level. Despite its exposed coastal position, the temple was undamaged by the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami. In 2016 it became the fourth Hindu temple in Tamil Nadu to receive ISO certification. The temple continues to be administered by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department of the Government of Tamil Nadu.

visitingInfo.entryRules: HR&CE operates separate free and paid darshan queues: the free queue is admitted until 7:30 PM, paid queue lines close at 6:30 PM, and a separate senior-citizen queue runs from 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM.
visitingInfo.officialContactNote: HR&CE publishes darshan hours and pooja timings on the temple's page at tiruchendurmurugan.hrce.tn.gov.in (temple id 38271). The department's postal address for the temple is Tiruchendur, Thoothukudi District 628215; confirm the day's schedule with the Executive Officer's office on +91-4639-242221, as timings extend during Vaikasi Visakam, Kantha Sashti and Thai Poosam.

openingHours.notes: HR&CE states the temple operates continuously from the 4:00 AM opening rite (Thirukkappu) to the 9:00–9:05 PM closing rite; the free darshan queue is admitted until 7:30 PM and paid queue lines close at 6:30 PM.

HR&CE indicates the temple may open as early as around 1:00 AM on major festival days such as Vaikasi Visakam and Kantha Sashti; exact festival-day timings were not independently quote-verified and should be reconfirmed before travel.
